docs.Title: Performance work statement: Enterprise IT Modernization Services
docs.Text:
## 1. Background
The applications run in two government data centers scheduled to close in FY28. Their hosting contract ends with the move. About a third have had no significant change in five years.

## 2. Objective
Move 140 mission applications from on-premises data centers to the Air Force cloud environment, keep each one authorized to operate throughout, and retire the applications that are no longer needed.

## 3. Scope
Rationalization, migration, platform engineering, cybersecurity and continuous ATO support, and program management, for a base year and four option years, with a 60-day transition-in.

## 4. Tasks
- Rationalize the portfolio: recommend retire, rehost, replatform or refactor for each application, with the evidence
- Migrate each application approved for migration, in waves the government approves
- Build and run the landing zone and DevSecOps pipelines the migrated applications use
- Keep every application authorized to operate: RMF packages, continuous monitoring, and POA&M closure
- Run a 60-day transition-in from the incumbent without a gap in hosting
- Manage the program: schedule, risks, monthly status and an integrated master schedule

## 5. Performance standards
- Migrated applications available during mission hours: 99.9% each month
- Applications keep their ATO through the move: No lapse
- Critical vulnerabilities fixed: Within 15 days, 95% of the time
- Deliverables on time and accepted on first submission: 90%

## 6. Deliverables
- Rationalization report, 90 days after award
- Wave migration plan, 30 days before each wave
- Monthly status report, 10th of each month
- Transition-in plan, 10 days after award

## 7. Place and period of performance
Contractor site, with on-site support at Maxwell AFB-Gunter Annex as needed. Base year and four 12-month options.

## 8. Security
Secret facility clearance; CUI throughout; DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC Level 2.

docs.Title: Quality assurance surveillance plan
docs.Text:
## 1. Purpose
How the COR checks each performance standard in the PWS, and what happens when one isn't met.

## 2. Surveillance
- Migrated applications available during mission hours: Monitoring data, monthly, acceptable quality level 99.9% each month
- Applications keep their ATO through the move: 100% inspection of each wave, acceptable quality level No lapse
- Critical vulnerabilities fixed: Scan data, monthly, acceptable quality level Within 15 days, 95% of the time
- Deliverables on time and accepted on first submission: COR review of each deliverable, acceptable quality level 90%

## 3. When a standard isn't met
The COR records it, the contractor gives a corrective action plan within 10 days, and repeated misses go into the CPARS evaluation.

docs.Title: Market research report
docs.Text:
## 1. Sources checked
- SAM.gov contract opportunities and entity registrations
- Prior Air Force and DoD awards for cloud migration (FPDS)
- GSA Multiple Award Schedule and the OASIS+ and Alliant 2 vehicles
- Industry day with 14 attendees, and a sources-sought notice with 11 responses

## 2. Commercial availability
Cloud migration and continuous ATO support are commercial services, sold in the form the Air Force needs.

## 3. Small business capability
Five of the 11 responses came from small businesses with relevant past performance of similar size; two had done migrations of more than 100 applications.

## 4. Conclusion
Full and open competition, with a recommendation to the Small Business Professional that the five capable small businesses be considered for a set-aside.

docs.Title: Independent government cost estimate
docs.Text:
## 1. Lines
- CLIN 0001: Application migration (140 applications), $9,200,000
- CLIN 0002: Platform engineering and DevSecOps, $6,100,000
- CLIN 0003: Cybersecurity and continuous ATO support, $4,300,000
- CLIN 0004: Program management, $2,600,000
- CLIN 0005: Transition-in and hypercare, $1,600,000

Total: $23,800,000 (base year and four options).

## 2. Basis
Labor hours by task from two comparable Air Force migrations, priced at GSA schedule rates for the labor categories, with 2% escalation each option year.

docs.Title: Acquisition strategy
docs.Text:
## 1. Contract type
Firm-fixed-price task order on a 5-year IDIQ: the work is defined by application and wave.

## 2. Competition
Full and open, best-value tradeoff. Technical is more important than management, then past performance; non-price factors together are significantly more important than price.

## 3. Set-aside
Unrestricted, after the Small Business Professional's review: the five capable small businesses could not show capacity for 140 applications in the schedule.

## 4. Schedule
Solicitation in October 2026; award in January 2027; transition-in complete in March 2027.

docs.Title: Section 508 accessibility determination
docs.Text:
## 1. Determination
The services deliver information and communication technology. The Revised 508 Standards apply to the applications as migrated and to every deliverable.

docs.Title: Small business coordination
docs.Text:
## 1. Review
Reviewed the market research and the five small business responses. Concur with the unrestricted strategy; a small business subcontracting plan with a 30% goal is required.

docs.Title: Funds certification
docs.Text:
## 1. Certification
Funds certified for the base year on purchase request F2KJ7A6101A001, $4,960,000. Option years are subject to the availability of funds.
